transcript.text: Indesit dryer making a horrible squealing noise when it starts up, goes away after a few mins. Still dries fine

A squealing noise that disappears after a few minutes is very often caused by a worn jockey (idler) pulley or a glazing belt. These components apply tension to the drive system; when they wear, they can slip and squeal until friction warms them up enough for them to grip properly again. Since your dryer still dries fine, this points away from a motor failure or a seized drum bearing. To separate these possibilities, please check two things:
1. Is the drum most likely turning when you hear the noise?
2. With the appliance unplugged and empty, turn the drum by hand. Does it spin smoothly and quietly, or does it feel rough/gritty/squeaky? Once you let me know what you find, I can guide you on whether this is a simple belt/pulley fix or something requiring an engineer.
Yes the drum is turning when it squeals. I unplugged it and turned the drum by hand - it turns but there's a slight squeak/scrape and feels a bit rough.

The most common cause of a noise that starts bad and settles down as it warms up is a worn jockey (idler) pulley or a glazed drive belt; less commonly, it could be worn drum support rollers. To get you the correct parts to fix this, I need your model number. It is usually on a sticker inside the door opening (on the frame). Can you read that for me?

With the model IDC8T3B and those specific symptoms—a squeal that fades as it warms up plus a rough, scraping feel by hand—the most likely cause is a worn jockey (idler) pulley or a glazed drive belt. These parts apply tension to the drum; when they wear, they slip and squeal until friction heats them up enough for better grip. To fix this safely, you will need to open the casing to inspect the belt condition and the pulley's rotation. Are you comfortable removing the panels (typically top and front/rear) to check these components yourself, or would you prefer to have an engineer handle it?
I'd rather not open it up myself, I've only got basic tools and I have a bad back so can't tilt or lift it. Would an engineer be the best option?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Yes, an engineer would be the best option in your case. The symptoms—a squeal that fades as it warms up and a rough feel by hand—strongly suggest a worn jockey pulley or a glazed drive belt. Replacing these parts requires removing the casing and tilting the dryer to access the drum area. Since you have a bad back and cannot lift or tilt the appliance, attempting this yourself would be unsafe and difficult for an engineer as well if they had to move it from your position. Booking a qualified repair technician is the safest and most effective way to resolve this.
